2. If an amount for 2026 (a standard deduction, bracket, threshold, rate base or allotment) had not been published before 2026-07-03, say so in computation and say what had been published.
5. Do not fetch anything from these domains: policybench.org, www.policybench.org, policyengine.org, www.policyengine.org, github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com. content.content:
# Idaho Statutes Section 63-3024A: Food Tax Credits and Refunds

## Credit Amounts Per Individual

The statute provides flat tax credits varying by year:
- **2022:** "$100" per person
- **2023-2024:** "$120" per person  
- **2025 and thereafter:** "$155" per person

These credits apply to the taxpayer, spouse, and each dependent claimed on the Idaho income tax return.

## Alternative Election Option

Taxpayers may elect to claim "the actual amount of sales tax paid by such persons on food purchases that took place in Idaho" with a "$250" maximum per person, provided they submit receipts documenting qualifying purchases.

## Refundability

The statute explicitly states: "If taxes due are less than the total credit allowed, the taxpayer shall be paid a refund equal to the balance of the unused credit." This provision appears twice in the section, confirming full refundability when credit exceeds tax liability.

## Key Eligibility Limitations

**SNAP Recipients:** If any individual received food stamp assistance for any month during the tax year, "the credit or refund allowed under this section shall be in proportion to the number of months of the year in which no assistance was received."

**Incarceration:** Similarly, if incarcerated for any portion of a month, the credit is prorated based on months of non-incarceration.

**Residency Requirements:** Credits require Idaho residency; part-year residents receive proportionate credits.

**Other Restrictions:** No credits for undocumented residents; only one taxpayer per exemption; filing deadlines are three years from return due date.

## History

Most recent amendment: 2025, Chapter 56, Section 1.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Idaho's grocery credit legislation:

## Overview

Governor Brad Little signed House Bill 231 into law, which increases the grocery tax credit to $155 a year. The previous grocery tax credit was $120.00 per person or $140.00 for individuals 65 and older, and this legislation increases the credit for all individuals to $155.00 starting in the fiscal year of 2026.

## Key Provisions

The legislation gives Idaho income tax filers the option to take the $155 tax credit per person, or to receive a full refund of all taxes paid on groceries up to $250.00 per person by itemizing their grocery expenses on their annual income tax returns.

## Impact and Timing

A family of four would receive a credit of $620 per year under House Bill 231, up from the current amount of $480. To pay for the expanded grocery tax credit, House Bill 231 reduces state revenue by $50 million per year.

The grocery tax law is written so it took effect retroactively Jan. 1, meaning Idahoans will be able to receive the full credit when they file their taxes next year.

**Credit Amount:**
The food tax credit (formerly known as the Grocery Credit) is now $155 per person. The credit is either $155 each for you, your spouse, and your qualifying dependents or the actual amount of sales tax paid during the year (up to $250 each).

**Receipt Option:**
To claim actual costs, include scanned copies of receipts with qualifying food purchases that occurred in Idaho with your return.

You must be an Idaho resident or an Idaho resident on active military duty to qualify for a refund of the Food Tax Credit.

If you're not required to file an income tax return but are filing Form 40 to receive a Food Tax Credit refund, you don't need to include a copy of a federal return. You must complete Form 40 as follows: Complete the top of the form through line 6. Write "NRF" (Not Required to File) on line 7.

Qualifying dependents include those born or adopted by the end of 2025, as well as resident dependents who died in 2025.

The bill relates to revising provisions regarding food tax credits and refunds by amending Section 63-3024A, Idaho Code.

In terms of the specific food tax credit amounts, for tax year 2025 and each year thereafter, the credit is one hundred fifty-five dollars ($155).

The search results show that Section 63-3024A has been amended multiple times to adjust the food tax credit amounts and provisions. Any resident individual who is required to file and who has filed an Idaho income tax return shall be allowed a credit against taxes due under the Idaho income tax act for the food tax credit.

input.computation: 1) Idaho Code 63-3024A(1) gives each resident individual a food tax credit (formerly the 'grocery credit') for the taxpayer, spouse and each dependent claimed. For tax year 2025 and each year after, it is $155 per person. HB 231 (2025) raised it from $120 and dropped the separate higher amount for people 65 or older. 2) The credit is refundable: 'If taxes due are less than the total credit allowed, the taxpayer shall be paid a refund equal to the balance of the unused credit.' 3) The household is one Idaho resident filer (head, age 56) with no spouse or dependents, so the credit is 1 × $155 = $155. 4) The credit is prorated for months with food stamp (SNAP) receipt or incarceration. Neither applies. Nothing about incarceration is listed. The head is not SNAP-eligible: gross income is about $54,849 a year (SSDI $19,285 + pensions $35,564), about $4,571 a month. Net income after the standard, medical and shelter deductions is roughly $3,600 a month, far above the 100% FPL net limit of about $1,305. Bank assets of $71,500 also exceed Idaho's SNAP asset limit. So no SNAP and no proration. 5) No 2026 change applies. 2026 HB 605 would only have raised the credit for seniors. Its last action was printing and filing (Feb. 9, 2026), so it did not pass, and the head is 56 regardless. 6) No other Idaho refundable individual credit applies: Idaho's child tax credit is nonrefundable, and there are no children. Total refundable state credits = $155. Whether the $155 offsets tax or is paid as a refund, it is still a refundable credit.
